name: swarmery-link
description: Mod (function hooks): reports this session's live state (turn start and end, tool calls by name and input hash, context fill, rate limits, cost) to a local swarmery daemon over its token-guarded link API, and switches itself off when the daemon's token file is absent. The sensor never blocks, changes or answers a hook's event. With the opt-in control option it also long-polls the daemon for this session's commands: stop aborts the running turn, prompt submits a prompt once the session is idle. With the opt-in forecast option it asks a small model, once per user turn and without holding the turn, what the turn will touch, and reports the forecast beside the actual (paths and numbers only) so the daemon can score its surprise. With the opt-in approvals option a permission ask goes to the swarmery approvals queue first and an AskUserQuestion can be answered from the dashboard; whenever the daemon is down or does not decide in time, the engine's own verdict, the hook shim or the native dialog takes over. With the opt-in swarm option it reports messages sent to and received from other sessions, claims each file the session starts editing in a registry shared by its sessions (a line beneath the answer when another live session edits the same file; with the opt-in claimConflicts option such a write is asked, or refused where no person would see the ask), and lets the dashboard send another session a message. With the opt-in planBand option it draws the session's plan phase and checklist above the prompt from the daemon's plan view, adds /plan, shows interview-style questions as a card and flags a turn that drifts off the phase.

control.title: Control from the dashboard
control.description: Let the swarmery dashboard stop this session's running turn and send it prompts. One background loop long-polls the daemon (loopback only, bearer token) for commands queued for this session alone; nothing runs inside a hook and no gating hook is registered. Off: no request goes to the command endpoints.

approvals.title: Approvals in Swarmery
approvals.description: Routes each permission ask to the Swarmery approvals queue first, ahead of the dialog or auto mode's classifier; the shim/dialog takes over if the daemon is down or does not decide in time. Only the engine's own ask goes there (its allow and deny stand), a production deploy is still confirmed in the terminal, and an AskUserQuestion can be answered from the dashboard. In auto mode this puts the ask to the dashboard before the classifier would have settled it. Off: no tool.check or AskUserQuestion hook is registered and no request goes to the permission endpoint.

planBand.title: Plan band
planBand.description: Show this session's swarmery plan phase in a band above the prompt (Phase n, its open criteria, [1] next phase, [2] open in Swarmery, [3] tick), add /plan [task-id] for the full checklist, draw a dashboard interview question (its JSON) as a card with the recommended option highlighted, and flag a turn that drifts off the phase with one line beneath its answer. Costs one small $.model.classify call per main-loop turn that edits files while a phase runs, plus a plan request (loopback, bearer token) at session start, after each turn and every 60 s. Off: no band, no command, no classification and no plan request.

swarm.title: Swarm coordination
swarm.description: Report messages this session sends to or receives from other sessions (text clipped to 4096 characters; a subagent's are left out), and claim each file the session starts editing in a registry its sessions share on this machine (paths and times only). When another live session holds the same file, a line beneath the answer says so; nothing is blocked. Claims are released at the end of each turn. With control on too, the dashboard can send another session a message. Off: no message hook, no registry access, no swarm events.

claimConflicts.title: Hold conflicting writes
claimConflicts.description: With swarm on: what happens when this session is about to Edit, Write, MultiEdit or NotebookEdit a file another live session holds a claim on. off: nothing is held, the line beneath the answer still says so. ask: the native permission dialog asks, naming the other session, in default/acceptEdits/plan; in auto/dontAsk/bypassPermissions, where no person would see the ask, the write is refused. deny: the write is refused in every mode. Bash commands are never checked (their target path cannot be read). With approvals on too, the ask goes to the Swarmery approvals queue first, as any ask does.

forecast.title: Turn forecast
forecast.description: Before each turn you type, ask haiku (one call, at most 300 output tokens, never waited on) which files the turn will touch, whether its tests will pass and how many steps it takes; at the turn's end report what it did. Both go to the daemon as paths and numbers only, never prompt text or tool input, and the dashboard's Insights shows how well the forecasts are calibrated. Off: no model call and no forecast events.

daemonUrl.title: Daemon URL
daemonUrl.description: The daemon's REST origin. Loopback http only (127.0.0.1, [::1] or localhost, any port); any other value is refused and the default is used, so the token never leaves the machine.
